Data.Name: initialText
Data.Data:
<size=20>Log:
 
Just after I'd landed and burrowed in with the deployment pods, a bearded man in a robe appeared and announced himself as 'the Good Wizard'. He waved his staff around and, as if by magic, the mountainside opened up and swallowed half of my base--The PCR with the power station and all the analysis equipment.

The 'wizard' claimed he needed to ‘confiscate’ the unit, muttering something about workings that must remain hidden. He then told me it was necessary that I bring others here to fulfill some kind of prophecy.

In any case, he left me stranded with just the long-range gateway module, so he'll get his wish whenever the next starship or station manages to pick up my distress signal. That may take a while, given how highly classified NT seemed to be keeping this operation...

In the meantime, I've wired up just enough emergency power to get the doors working in order to scout the area.

Notes:
There's a village to the south.
A retired adventurer lives in the northwest.
The mountain passes here are constantly being blocked by rock slides. If the grass is still fresh under a rock pile, the rocks fell recently.</size>

The M.O.R.O.N. includes state-of-the-art scanning and material sampling equipment, along with all other necessary modules as configured for your mission. Your M.O.R.O.N. loadout: [Chassis ELT - Dual Bay] Entry, Landing, Self-Tunneling Installation and Seclusion | [Module GCU] Gateway Teleportation System - Communications Array - Utility Hatch | - Configuration Option: Iron Outer Hatch - Manual Operation | [Module PCR] Power - Computerized Analysis - Research Important! Before beginning M.O.R.O.N. operation, read the included Operator's Manual: M.O.R.O.N. We thank you for your purchase, and wish you the best of luck on your M.O.R.O.N. mission.

Data.Name: initialText
Data.Data:
<size=22><color=#00dccf>Greetings, Captain! I proffer my apologies for disassembling your impressive machine-comet. You've perhaps already seen too much, but your coming was necessary and our interlopers have now departed. You see, there were forces at work here you are not meant to know! Besides, what's half a M.O.R.O.N. to a megacorp like yours? ;)</size><size=14>

</size><size=22>Therefore, I hope you will forgive my tampering in your affairs and accept the safe return of your device and the enjoyment of my bar. Drinks are on the house.</size><size=14>

</size><size=22>But now I must ask one last thing of you: Fulfill the Prophecy. Bring forth the crown, conduct the Ceremony of Crowning, and give this land a King!</color>
<color=#14ec7a>Please use the attached script to conduct the Ceremony.</color></size><size=14>

</size><size=22><color=#a3a3a3>(As the highest in rank among your group, your duties and destiny lie along another path and thus you cannot become King.)</color></size><size=14>

</size><size=22><color=#00dccf>Cordially,
The Good Wizard</color></size>

Data.Data:
<size=20><color=#14ec7a>[ CEREMONY OF CROWNING ~ CAPTAIN'S SCRIPT ]</color></size><size=10>

</size><size=20><color=#0745e2>- HARK! / HARK YE!
- Let the Ceremony of Crowning begin!
- Who doth contend for the crown? Say “I doth.”</color></size><size=10>

</size><size=20><color=#a3a3a3>(Pause for doths. Anyone who doesn't say “I doth” is disqualified.)</color></size><size=10>

</size><size=20><color=#0745e2>- Lay thy treasures before thee.</color></size><size=10>

</size><size=20><color=#a3a3a3>(One at a time, ask each adventurer to describe the treasure he or she has won.)</size><size=10>

</size><size=20><color=#0745e2>- (NAME), Tell the tale of thy Treasure</color></size><size=10>

</size><size=20>(Take a moment to decide who rightfully bears the Best Treasure based on story, apparent value, and any [ OFFICIAL RULES ] in the treasures' descriptions.)</color></size><size=10>

</size><size=20><color=#0745e2>- I, the Crownbearer, have chosen.
- I DUB THEE, (NAME), KING OF MYSTIC VALLEY!</color></size><size=10>

</size><size=20><color=#a3a3a3>(Present the Crown to the new king.)</size><size=10>

</size><size=14>(The King now rules this domain. As captain, you are to extend all diplomatic courtesy to the new King. The King may of course join you on the departures shuttle as well to come and establish diplomatic relations and the terms of his/her surrender to Nanotrasen. You may also assist the new king with slaying the remaining evil forces who invaded when the Tower was awakened.</size></color><size=10>

</size><size=20><color=#00dccf>*** <3 THE END <3 ***</color></size>

Data.Name: initialText
Data.Data:
<size=18>Tower Commander -</size><size=12>

</size><size=18>Your mission is as follows: Stop the intruders from reaching the rooftop, fulfilling the Prophecy, or living to tell of it--Your choice.</size><size=12>

</size><size=18>The green lights along the north wall of this room show the progress of intruders through the Tower, allowing estimation of their position.</size><size=12>

</size><size=18>Lights at the left and right ends of this room show the status of the Tower's power systems and the 9F defense system, respectively.</size><size=12>

</size><size=18>Two rooms to the south will open once certain points in the Tower have been breached. The buttons within each room can be used to deploy a one-time wave of defense forces to a selected floor.</size><size=12>

</size><size=18>The teleporter room to the north provides teleportation to destinations that become available based on intruders' progress through the Tower. They are one-way. The final teleporter leads to a ready room for a final showdown on the Tower roof which will become available when intruders on the roof open the final seal and are set to fulfil the Prophecy. Be ready to engage at a moment's notice if you select this option.</size><size=12>

</size><size=18>Remember, time is money. Every additional hour you can buy adds to our bottom line--and your bonus!</size><size=12>

</size><size=18>- Management</size>

Data.Name: initialText
Data.Data: Project Trickster: Final Report The Mystic Valley planetoid was artificially constructed by a secretive alien race with advanced genetic engineering capabilities. They designed its geology and ecosystem to cultivate a species of humanoids infused with genetic material stolen from a line of space wizards, their apparent goal being the generation and study of magical phenomena. Their deliberate amplification of these genes within the catalytic environment produced a concentration of magical energies in the tiny planetoid, causing it to manifest divine and demonic activity and attracting the attention of the magically-attuned and corporations with advanced scanning instruments, among whom we were fortunately the first. While we initially approached with caution, after extensive (and expensive) scouting, we found the alien species sought to remain hidden and avoid all contact, and so we proceeded to the next phase of the operation. The Good Wizard, likely sent by the Wizard Federation to contain this debacle, arrived early in our operation's timeline and immediately began stirring various changes in the site's energies and rallying its people. He seeks to stop the experiment and bring the land's out-of-control magical forces into a harmonious balance. He thus estabished the Prophecy, by which the people of the land will conquer its evils and gain a King, and their allegiance to him or her will supposedly focus their aggregated magical energies into a stable, neutral form. Given that we here at the so-called Tower of Trickery are paid extremely well to extract the chaotic energies and exotic materials this place generates on behalf of those who know their worth, we seek to delay this eventuality as long as we can. Nevertheless, the Wizard's sole possession of magical knowledge leaves us without recourse but to play our role as the incarnation of deceit in the realm's mythos for as long as we still can. It was only a matter of time before Nanotrasen lucked into picking up some kind of signal from this place, and they recently sent a small research probe to land on the planetoid (which almost immediately ceased functioning. Ha!) Where NT goes, its rivals follow. The cat is out of the bag and it's likely events are about to come to a head. It's been a good (and handsomely profitable) run.

Data.Name: initialText
Data.Data: Anomaly codename ‘ECCom’ is unexplained. We hypothesize it to be the result of a magical accident involving a formerly Nanotrasen-affiliated conscript we utilized in preliminary scouting of the planetoid's dangerous areas. We're still figuring out what to tell the higher-ups about that one.
